subtitle: Generic plan.md example
title: CSV Export for Order History
lead: Open points extracted from plan.md (v0.1.0). Team roles, colors, and constraints come from the reusable context.json.

keystone.openBanner: Decide first: Synchronous download vs. asynchronous background job. This determines whether row-cap and timeout limits apply.
keystone.mootBanner: Async background job selected: synchronous row-limit questions are greyed out, and Platform must be consulted on queue/worker infra.

questions.title: Synchronous download vs. asynchronous job
questions.question: How should the CSV export be generated and delivered to the customer?
questions.context: plan.md §3 (OQ-1) and §2 (U-1: 'must feel fast'). No delivery mechanism is specified yet.
options: Synchronous HTTP download directly from the Order History page
Asynchronous background job that emails a download link when ready
questions.reason: Requires no queue or email infrastructure and matches typical B2C order counts; revisit if exports routinely exceed 5,000 rows.

questions.title: Maximum rows for synchronous export
questions.question: What hard row limit should apply to a single synchronous CSV download?
questions.context: plan.md §3 (OQ-2). Needed to turn U-1 ('feel fast') into a testable bound.
options: Up to 5,000 rows (show prompt to narrow date filter above limit)
Up to 1,000 rows (show prompt to narrow date filter above limit)
questions.reason: 5,000 rows serialize in under 500 ms and cover 99% of customer histories without risking gateway timeouts.

questions.title: PII fields in exported CSV
questions.question: Should customer PII (shipping street, phone number) be included in the CSV?
questions.context: plan.md §1 lists order number, date, amount, currency, status. §3 (OQ-3) asks whether shipping address/phone should also be exported.
options: Exclude shipping street and phone number (keep only plan.md §1 columns)
Include full shipping address and phone number
questions.reason: Follows data minimization (GDPR) and avoids exporting extra PII into local spreadsheets.

questions.title: CSV encoding and delimiter
questions.question: Which character encoding and delimiter does our target accounting/Excel setup expect?
questions.context: plan.md §3 (OQ-4). Fact question depending on customer/accounting tools.
options: UTF-8 with BOM and semicolon (;) — standard for German/EU Excel
UTF-8 without BOM and comma (,) — RFC 4180 standard
questions.reason: No proposal: fact question — Business/Operations knows which locale and import tools customers use.
